name: Diurnal-Scaled Range Breakout
note: Every 5-minute slot of the day gets its own volatility unit D_s -- the median high-low range of that same clock slot over the previous N sessions -- and both the breakout buffer and the risk are quoted in D_s, so a 12-cent midday break and a 40-cent opening break are the same event. The regular session is located from the tape's own volume profile rather than assumed, so it is right in either DST; the stop/target/trail are carried in exit_signal because the whole point is that they re-scale with the clock rather than with a flat ATR.
source: Andersen & Bollerslev, "Intraday periodicity and volatility persistence in financial markets," Journal of Empirical Finance 4(2-3), 1997, 115-158; Andersen, Bollerslev, Dobrev & co-authors, "Time-Varying Periodicity in Intraday Volatility," CREATES RP 2018-05 (pure.au.dk/ws/files/120472862/rp18_05.pdf)
